key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, travel speed, and welding current affect molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These parameter trends can guide weld optimization for low-thermal-expansion Invar structures used in aerospace composite molds.
method: Parameter variation: 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min travel speed, and 150–170 A current
evidence_signal: Within the tested ranges, higher power increased penetration and keyhole size, higher speed reduced penetration and weld width, and higher current widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract provides parameter trends but no quantitative validation errors or mechanical-property results, limiting confidence in extrapolation beyond the studied ranges.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
